hi Jami,
 you should try to read your data set into R wth read.csv and see if it coereces all of the variables to factors. [can you provide your data set for me to look at?]. 
 
The default parameterization is log(E[N]) and logit(p) (Ian can correct me if thats wrong).  So you need to exp() the intercept to get "individuals per location" and
exp(intercept)/(1+exp(intercept)) to get the baseline detection probability.  This is why negative estimates are allowed.
 
regards,
andy

parts:
Hi Jami-

I had some similar problems with csv formatting but my discrete number
(e.g., year 2000, 2001, 2002) data columns were being read as
continuous. I tried specifying the discrete, categorical, continuous
variables with something like

dataobject$categoricalsitecovariate=factor(dataobject
$categoricalsitecovariate)

or

dataobject$categoricalsitecovariate=as.numeric(dataobject
$categoricalsitecovariate)

but those variables were still read as continuous so I just converted,
for example, years 2000-2001 to years a-b, or year post-management
(ypm) 1-7 as a-g in the csv. The other problem I had was correctly
distinguishing the site- and obs-level covariates in the umf, so I
reformatted my csv files to "wide" format, like the widewt example
file in the csv folder of Unmarked, and then everything worked fine.

So here's some example data from a csv:

site y.1 y.2 y.3 area hab ypm year obs.1
obs.2 obs.3
Aichele 1 0 0 60275 TH f a DS DS DS
Aichele 0 1 1 60275 TH g b DS DS RZ
Balicki 0 0 0 79190 NH d a JM JM JM
Balicki 0 0 0 79190 NH e b KG KG DS

and here's a sample of my R code:

### load Unmarked package
library(unmarked)
### select a species csv datafile for abundance modeling and convert
to unmarked dataframe (umf) object
umf=csvToUMF("BOBO SK.csv",long=FALSE,type="unmarkedFramePCount")
### summarize model variables in umf
summary(umf)
### Observer-specific detection parameter, mng type and ypm abundance
parameters, and sampling-area offsets
year=pcount(~obs ~year+offset(log(area)),umf)
mng=pcount(~obs ~mng+year+offset(log(area)),umf)
ypm=pcount(~obs ~ypm+year+offset(log(area)),umf)
global=pcount(~obs ~mng+ypm+year+offset(log(area)),umf)
models=fitList(year,mng,ypm,global)
modSel(models)
summary(global)

Matt

parts:
Hi Jami -

Just a couple more points:

You might try reading your data into R manually (with read.csv) as Andy suggested and then create your unmarkedFrame either directly with unmarkedFrameOcc() or with other helper functions that work on data frames (formatWide() and formatLong()).

Also, regarding what scale results are on, you can use the backTransform() methods to get predictions back in the bounded scale.

Best,
Ian

--
Ian Fiske
PhD Candidate
Department of Statistics
North Carolina State University

parts:
Hi Jamie -- see below for comments.

On Wed, Mar 17, 2010 at 1:22 PM, Jami <octop...@yahoo.com> wrote:
HI Ian,
Thanks for your help.

I am trying to read my .csv file per your suggestion. I am following
the example for the wt dataset given in the Overview of Unmarked.
The
data is in long form (i.e. vertical columns for each variable). I am
assuming that the argument direction="long" accounts for this format.
What is input into the argument for varying?  I tried many things and
got the following error message:  ## Error in guess(varying) : Failed
to guess time-varying variables from their names##

The help for the reshape function will explain the reshape function (direction="long" converts to long).  The Overview is working to get a wide data set into long because unmarked uses a long format.  If you already have a long format, then skip the reshape function in the Overview and try formatLong -- see the help on that.  You might want to read the help on unmarkedFrame too.

Also in the wt example what does the script "obsCov[order(obsCov
$id...)" do?

This line is reordering the observations so that obs per site varies fastest and site varies slowest by row -- in other words you want something like:

site obs
1    1
1    2
2    1
2    2

I included my script below incase that will help.
Thanks for your help.
Jami

My Script
test<-read.csv("MasterUnmarkedTestVols2009.csv", sep=",", head=T)
y<-test[,3]
siteCovs<-test[,c("VS", "CliffVS")]
obsCovs<-reshape(test[, c("StartTime", "BinocPower", "BinocView",
"ScopePower", "ScopeView", "Temp", "Sky", "Wind", "ObsRankNoVIP",
"ExpRank", "SiteVisits", "PercentMov", "WeightedVis", "DomFeat")],
varying= 1:14,  direction="long")


## Error in guess(varying) :
 Failed to guess time-varying variables from their names

We would need to see some example data to help with any more specifics with your case.
 
Best,
Ian

--
Ian Fiske
PhD Candidate
Department of Statistics
North Carolina State University
